messages:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert for tenant 'zenith' in eu2 — elevated 5xx rate (~26%) and tail latency > 2s. Routing spikes observed from zenith-eu2-dedicated pool. Paging oncall: @Sara P., @Miguel R.

Sara P.: I'm on it. Looking at traces — spikes started ~14:03 UTC. Quick check: not seeing obvious model OOMs yet, could be hot shard or network flapping.

Miguel R.: Oncall here. Zenith is on a dedicated pool (zenith-eu2-dedicated). Warm standby pool (zenith-eu2-warm) is provisioned and healthy. I can initiate warm cutover if needed.

Kevin L.: Quick Q — do we prefer L7 reroute (fast) or DNS failover (slower)? L7 avoids TTL waiting.

Maria T.: Customer has VPC peering + managed DNS. Need Zenith SRE signoff for any DNS swap. I'll DM them now.

Oncall Bot: Channel created: #inc-zenith-eu2-2445009999

Miguel R.: Proposed mitigation plan:
1) Canary 10% -> zenith-eu2-warm
2) Monitor error rate for 2 minutes
3) If stable, ramp to 50% then 100%
4) Prepare DNS TTL reduction to 30s if we decide full DNS cutover

Sara P.: Agreed. Start canary via routing tool. Keep me posted on 5xx delta.

Eng-Rel: Executing routing shift (command):
```
ri route shift --tenant zenith --from zenith-eu2-dedicated --to zenith-eu2-warm --percent 10 --reason "5xx spike"
```

Deploy Bot: Shift initiated (task id 0x9f4b).

Miguel R.: Canary live at 14:18 UTC — 10% traffic -> warm. Monitoring dashboards in #infra-metrics.

Sara P.: Canary metrics: canary 5xx = 1.2% (baseline 0.6%), latency median for canary improved from 320ms -> 210ms. Canary error slightly higher but within expected variability.

Kevin L.: Looks ok. If canary holds, ramp slowly. Also prepare SRV/CNAME change snippet for DNS team.

Maria T.: Zenith SRE (zenith-sre) confirmed peering fallback allowed. They asked to wait until >=50% before any DNS swap.

Miguel R.: Ramping to 50% now.

Miguel R.: 50% at 14:28 UTC. Observations: errors on warm ~0.8%. Dedicated pool CPU is pegged on a subset of workers — likely hot shard.

Sara P.: I'm going to drain the hottest worker on the dedicated pool to rebalance. Running: 
```
ri pool drain --pool zenith-eu2-dedicated --selector worker-7 --grace 90
```

Eng-Rel: Draining worker-7. Monitoring redistribution and queue lengths.

Jess O.: Taking over oncall (handoff) — 14:40 UTC. Thanks Sara/Miguel for initial triage.

Sara P.: Handing off. Remaining actions: continue ramp to 100% if stable, coordinate DNS TTL to 30s and SRV failover with Maria, confirm customer comms.

Jess O.: Acknowledged. I'll watch rollback triggers and be primary for customer updates.

Network Ops Bot: Route53 change prepared by Maria T.:
```
- zone: zenith.prod
- change: CNAME zenith.api -> zenith-eu2-warm.edge.redwood.net
- ttl: 30
```

Maria T.: Holding DNS change until we hit >=75% or customer says go. Zenit SRE wants a soft cutover first.

Miguel R.: 75% at 14:49 UTC. Error rate steady ~0.7%. CPU on dedicated pool decreasing after drain. Warm pool handling load well.

Jess O.: Proceeding to 100% ramp unless anyone objects.

Deploy Bot: Ramp complete: 100% traffic -> zenith-eu2-warm at 14:55 UTC. Task id 0x9f4b.

Oncall Bot: Incident update: mitigation in place, customer impact reduced. Paging suppressed.

Zenith-SRE: Thanks — we see traffic normalized and edge latency back to expected. We'll keep peering route active for 2 hours for safety.

Jess O.: Post-cutover checks: healthchecks green, error budget within threshold, no new 5xx alarms for 15m. Marking mitigated and beginning incident write-up.

Jess O.: Initial action items for postmortem (assignments tentative):
- Rerun load tests on dedicated pool to reproduce hot-shard (owner: Eng-Rel)
- Improve autoscaling policy and shard redistribution (owner: Eng-Rel)
- Document DNS cutover playbook with TTL preflight (owner: Network Ops)
- Validate warm pool autoscaling and faster readiness (owner: Infra)

Eng-Rel: I'll own autoscaling and hot-shard investigation.

Sara P.: Note for impact: customer reported slow SSO (auth) for ~3 minutes during the ramp window; include in customer impact blurb.

Jess O.: Drafting initial customer summary: "We observed elevated 5xx errors from the dedicated pool starting ~14:03 UTC due to a hot worker causing resource contention. We performed a controlled routing cutover to the warm standby pool and completed traffic shift by 14:55 UTC. Total customer-facing degradation lasted ~52 minutes. Root cause investigation ongoing; follow-up postmortem to be posted."

Oncall Bot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident owner: Jess O. Postmortem assigned to Eng-Rel, due in 48h.

Sara P.: Thanks everyone. I'll close the channel after handoff. :white_check_mark:
